article.title: A Small Habit, A Big Change
article.content: Big goals are exciting, but tiny habits are what move you forward every day. Suppose you want to improve your English speaking. Instead of waiting for a free hour, try five minutes daily. Read one paragraph aloud, record your voice, and listen to it again. You will notice pronunciation issues that are easy to ignore in real conversations. The key is consistency, not intensity. A small habit removes the pressure of perfection and lowers the chance of quitting. After a few weeks, your confidence grows naturally. The progress may seem slow, but it is steady and reliable. Most long term growth begins with simple actions repeated many times.
article.translation: 宏大目标很令人兴奋，但真正推动你每天前进的是微小习惯。假设你想提升英语口语，与其等一个完整小时，不如每天练五分钟：朗读一段文字，录下自己的声音，再回听一遍。你会发现许多在真实对话中容易忽略的发音问题。关键是持续，而不是强度。小习惯能减轻“必须完美”的压力，也会降低放弃概率。几周后，你的自信会自然增长。进步看起来可能不快，但稳定且可靠。大多数长期成长，都始于被反复执行的简单动作。

questions.prompt: Which action does the article suggest for speaking practice?
options: Wait until you have a free hour
Record a short reading and listen again
Speak only when pronunciation is perfect
questions.explanation: 文中建议每天五分钟，朗读一段、录音并回听。

questions.prompt: What does the writer consider most important?
questions.explanation: “The key is consistency, not intensity”强调持续练习。

questions.prompt: Why can a small habit be easier to maintain?
options: It reduces pressure and the chance of quitting
questions.explanation: 小习惯减轻追求完美的压力，降低放弃的概率。
